chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Isa ibn Sabih, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the pickpocket, the grave-digger, and the snatcher, so he said: “The pickpocket and the grave-digger have their hand cut off, but the snatcher does not have his hand cut off.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What is indicated by this report and the hadith of Mansur, that the pickpocket’s hand is cut off, is to be understood as applying when he steals from the lower garment. But if he steals from the upper garment, then cutting off his hand is not required, according to what al-Sakuni and Mism'a Abu Sayyar explained in their two narrations from Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ الْأَسْفَلِ: the lower garment, from which theft entails the stricter ruling here
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ الْأَعْلَى: the upper garment, from which theft does not entail cutting in this clarification
key_terms.الطَّرَّارِ: the pickpocket; one who stealthily steals from a person’s garment
key_terms.النَّبَّاشِ: the grave-digger or grave-plunderer; one who exhumes graves to steal
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِسِ: the snatcher; one who seizes property quickly without the full conditions of secret theft
key_terms.قَطْعُهُ: the cutting off of his hand as a hadd punishment
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the legal punishment of hand-cutting is applied

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the pickpocket, grave-digger, and snatcher in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses legal rulings concerning different forms of theft: pickpocketing, grave-plundering, and snatching. It states that the hadd applies to the pickpocket and the grave-digger, but not to the snatcher, and it further clarifies that the ruling on the pickpocket depends on the specific manner and location of the theft.
